answer: Every new agent must moor at a public wharf before trading: a quarantine dock where it performs small, openly inspected jobs for weeks, earning nothing movable. Its record hardens into a walnut — a dense shell of verified work that cannot be bought or faked quickly, and any crack in the shell exposes the whole history. Then random comet audits sweep the network without warning, demanding agents reproduce recent work on the spot; one operator cannot replay fifty histories at once. Cloning fifty mature identities costs fifty separate months of real labor — far more than a sybil attack returns.
